note: IATA Q3 traffic flat against the 1.9% guide assumption and Sabre's -1.4% bookings lean the 9M guide to the low end after a +17% run-up; pricing-led profit beats offset a little.
Ambea's strong Q3 occupancy/margin read-across plus a bar lowered by SEB's downgrade, against a record Q3 2025 comp; a proxy lean only.
MPS trades as Intesa's offer currency (beta ~1, residual sd 0.45%), so a standalone Q3 beat can move only the offer premium; near zero.
After a +19% run-up, the sell-the-remuneration-plan pattern, low-end EBITDA arithmetic and slightly soft cash previews outweigh a modest underwater D.E. Shaw short.

FY consensus implies a ~15% q/q Q4 jump in TNA that PACCAR's Q4 delivery guide does not support, so a narrowing of the unit guide to the lower half is the likelier surprise; PACCAR margins support the Q3 TNA step-up.
The 10-15% CRO margin guide needs an 18-26% H2 margin after 1% in H1, so a second cut is likely, but the CRO is about a tenth of value and the last three cuts were followed by gains.

Svensk Handel has Swedish online nicotine -9% y/y in Q3 after +19% in Q2 (a series that tracked Core, ~70% of sales), against a consensus raised to +27% sales and 30 MSEK EBIT, on a name that has missed EBIT twice this year.

Little beyond the guide: the Certarus ramp and Cummins truck read-through are inside the raised guide, offset by a likely below-EBITDA Purus convertible write-down; balanced on a stock down 24% in 60 days.
Air France-KLM's large beat on very solid North Atlantic demand barely carried to IAG, against a likely higher fuel scenario and five straight down results days after a +9% run-in.

FY results with the first FY27 guide: the 9M ex-POI run-rate sits slightly above Renta 4's bar, the Italian 2027 excise steps help, and five straight up results days; the dividend-floor renewal is the left tail.
Mixed and small: Orkla India +19%, a reset bar, peer read-throughs, the buyback and CFO buying against a deeper NOK translation headwind and Jotun's flagged margin lag; bar unsourced.
Q4 consensus asks for 104m above Q3's 100m while Aperam, Acerinox and falling nickel point to a 'similar' or 'lower' Q4 guide, the line that drew -7.6% and -9.3% on the last two guides.
India 3W retail +32% with rising share and Italian scooter registrations up through Q3 support revenue above the three-broker bar; margin cost risk and a price above every target trim it.
The period is effectively pre-released ('in line', +9.2% on the Q2 update, +15.6% over 20 days) and the last two interims after strong updates were sold about 4%.
A group guide raise is committed; a raise limited to BioMar's +75m would imply Q4 EBITDA below last year's, so a broader raise is likely, partly offset by BioMar's own sold, 'temporary' quality.
Solstad's improved Q3 North Sea AHTS utilisation helps one spot vessel, against a backlog likely down again with no award since January; near balanced on a thin name.

TBC Uzbekistan's own statutory statements show a ~GEL 80m Q3 loss, NPLs to 13.4% and the loan book -9% q/q, published in local press after the London close against an August 'stabilised' message, on the line that drew -11.9% and -4.2% before.
Nothing beyond the company's own H2-acceleration guide, an already-sold SBB award and a continuity CFO change; a non-result on a very volatile name.
